Messages.Author: joseph mcevoy
Messages.Body:
Ok.. I asked earlier if a person who is playing a Malkavian deck can
bleed his prey during somebody else's turn, then play a Major Boon to cancel
the bleed and take the bleed himself.

This was deemed ok. Now, here's the senario:

I'm playing Malkavian. Steve, my prey, has finished the action
phase of his round. I send in Gilbert to bleed ala Maddness Network.
Am I allowed to use Action Cards, such as Night Moves (+3/+6 stealth) or
does it have to be a 'cardless' action? Also, since it is Steve's turn, is
he allowed to block the action, play reaction cards, and so forth?

For the sake of the example, lets say it's an ordinary bleed and
Steve chooses not to block. I then toss down Major Boon to "take another
Methuselah's blood pool loss due to a bleed (must be at least one blood).
Modifiers to the bleed can be played after you play this card." Then, I
toss down Spying Mission, which says "Only usable when bleeding. Instead of
removing pool from the Methuselah you are bleeding, put this card on the
acting vampire. Next time this vampire bleeds the same Methuselah, burn
this card for +2 bleed."

First, is this a legal move? Second, who does the +2 bleed modifier
apply to, me or Steve? Thirdly, since I played Major Boon to take the
damage done by the bleed, and this new modifier says that no pool damage is
being done, do I lose the one pool?

The group I play with tend to be VERY picky about combos like
this... and instead of tossing this in and getting into an arguement that
goes longer than the game itself I wanted some official rulings first.

Besides, I need something to counter Steve's Gangrel/Dominate/S:CE
deck... :-)

Joseph.

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <43clv1$g...@motss.newpaltz.edu>, mcev...@matrix.newpaltz.edu
(joseph mcevoy) wrote:
: I'm playing Malkavian. Steve, my prey, has finished the action

: phase of his round. I send in Gilbert to bleed ala Maddness Network.
: Am I allowed to use Action Cards, such as Night Moves (+3/+6 stealth) or
: does it have to be a 'cardless' action? Also, since it is Steve's turn, is
: he allowed to block the action, play reaction cards, and so forth?

He is allowed to try and block the action, but according to the DTR, he
cannot play reaction cards. Also, because it is your turn, you cannot
play action cards. So a Night Moves would be out, and votes, but you
could try to equip or retain a retainer or employ a minion.

: For the sake of the example, lets say it's an ordinary bleed and

: Steve chooses not to block. I then toss down Major Boon to "take another
: Methuselah's blood pool loss due to a bleed (must be at least one blood).
: Modifiers to the bleed can be played after you play this card." Then, I
: toss down Spying Mission, which says "Only usable when bleeding. Instead of
: removing pool from the Methuselah you are bleeding, put this card on the
: acting vampire. Next time this vampire bleeds the same Methuselah, burn
: this card for +2 bleed."

Well, I started to say that you would not be able to use a Spying Mission,
as the Major Boon Master card would stop the action ala Brujah Frenzy
ending the action and no other action modifiers are allowed. But, Major
Boon specifically states that the bleed can be modified. So playing a
spying mission would be legal, but I would see no point. I believe that
the Spying Mission would apply to you (the acting Meth.) This is from the
sense of a Conditioning would cause you to lose additional blood. When you
accept a Major Boon bleed, you are taking all of the effects on to
yourself, and that would include IMO the affects of a Spying Mission.

Honestly, I do not know what the official ruling would be, but that is my
take on it.

I hope this helps

stephen

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
In article <43clv1$g...@motss.newpaltz.edu> mcev...@matrix.newpaltz.edu (joseph mcevoy) writes:

> The group I play with tend to be VERY picky about combos like
>this... and instead of tossing this in and getting into an arguement that
>goes longer than the game itself I wanted some official rulings first.

Jyhad was originally a very good game system. It has its nice, `regular'
combos - such as Flash + Throw Sewer Lid + Growing Fury + Nimble Feet
+ Growing Fury + ... It is due to a number of DTR mis-rules and a
few ill-conceived cards that gives power to these Mt$-like combos
in Jyhad.

> Besides, I need something to counter Steve's Gangrel/Dominate/S:CE
>deck... :-)

First, Protean untaps are underpriced and subject to abuse. (If they've
got an interesting card idea, they don't have to make the card cost-free.)
Second, that deck is very easy to counter: just Suddenly Reverse his
Dominate skill cards. It's worth it to put 10 SR's in your deck to
make 20 cards in his deck unplayable.

I understand that it is very hard for Mt$ players to use an SR on
`something as trivial as a skill card', preferring to save them to
ruin mega-combos such as Minion Tap + Golconda + Soul Gem. However,
as for me, if I have an SR in my hand, I'll undoubtedly SR any
Dominate card dropped by a Gangrel player, or any Protean card
dropped by a non-Gangrel player. SR on sight, no questions asked.
If I SR'ed 3 or 4 skill cards in a row, I'll SR any Barrens, too :-)

> I'm playing Malkavian. Steve, my prey, has finished the action

> he allowed to block the action, play reaction cards, and so forth?

The last rulings I saw about MN were that it's still Steve's turn:
1. You may not play action cards
2. He may not play reaction cards

I don't know about action modifiers...
Combat cards are allowed, however!

a directed bleed, for example computer hacking, now you can bleed your

Messages.Body:
Harald AAberg <gk...@student.adb.gu.se> wrote:
>That might be so but actually a smarter move, as I see it would be to use
>a directed bleed, for example computer hacking, now you can bleed your
>predator. Then reduce the bleed to 1 with telepatic (...aaah I forgot, is

>it telepatic counter?) and take it with your major boon...

This doesn't work for three reasons: You can only react to others' actions,
you cannot play reactions during your turn, and you can only use Telepathic
Counter when you are the one being bled (card text).
